bug_description.normalized: The saved `poc` radio frame reaches `Leader::HandleServerData()`, where `ThreadTlv::GetTlv(..., kThreadNetworkData, ...)` extracts a `ThreadNetworkDataTlv` whose nested stable `PrefixTlv` carries `mPrefixLength = 0x85`. `HandleServerData()` forwards that raw network-data buffer into `RegisterNetworkData(HostSwap16(aMessageInfo.mPeerAddr.mFields.m16[7]), ...)`, coupling it with the sender-derived peer RLOC16. `RegisterNetworkData()` first gates storage through `RlocLookup(..., kMatchModeRloc16, false)`: in that admission pass, vulnerable `PrefixTlv::IsValid()` only checks that the TLV body is long enough for `BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength)` bytes and omits the fixed 16-byte `Ip6::Address` bound added by the patch. Because that predicate still returns true for `mPrefixLength = 0x85` (`BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) == 17`), the crashing path remains viable if the included `HasRoute` entry matches the derived peer RLOC16. When storage proceeds, `AddPrefix()` repeats the same `aPrefix.IsValid()` check and then dispatches the `HasRoute` sub-TLV to `AddHasRoute()`, which copies the malformed prefix length and prefix bytes into persistent leader network-data state. Registration signals `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA`; `HandleNetworkDataUpdateRouter()` then builds `static const uint8_t tlvs[] = {Tlv::kNetworkData}`, constructs the 16-byte stack destination `ff02::1`, and calls `SendDataResponse(destination, tlvs, sizeof(tlvs), delay)`. The `Tlv::kNetworkData` case resolves neighbor information via `GetNeighbor(destination)`, which consults `LeaderBase::GetContext(destination, context)`. `GetContext()` passes the persisted overlong prefix length and the 16-byte destination buffer into `NetworkData::PrefixMatch()`. There, `bytes = BitVectorBytes(aLength)` becomes 17 and the compare loop executes `diff = a[i] ^ b[i]`; when `i == 16`, it reads one byte past the end of `destination`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ at `src/core/thread/network_data.cpp:917`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed path that extracts attacker-controlled Thread Network Data from the received radio frame into a parser-visible object.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a crafted radio frame delivered through `otPlatRadioReceiveDone()` after the harness has enabled Thread and made the instance leader. In the saved bytes, the relevant payload contains a Thread TLV header `0x0a 0x23`; its nested Prefix TLV begins `0x03 0x21 0x20 0x85`, so the extracted `networkData` buffer already carries the stable Prefix TLV and overlong prefix-length byte later reused on the crashing path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The embedded Prefix TLV bytes, including the attacker-controlled prefix-length field later exposed as `mPrefixLength`, originate in the raw Network Data buffer passed into `RegisterNetworkData`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `PrefixMatch()` indexes into the 16-byte destination address with an attacker-derived byte count larger than 16 and reads past the stack `destination` object.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/core/thread/network_data.cpp:917:23` and identifies `destination` in `HandleNetworkDataUpdateRouter()` as the overflown stack object.

root_cause.code: return ((GetLength() >= sizeof(*this) - sizeof(NetworkDataTlv)) && (GetLength() >= BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) + sizeof(*this) - sizeof(NetworkDataTlv)));
root_cause.description: The Prefix TLV validator checks that the TLV body is long enough for the advertised prefix bytes, but it omits the fixed-size safety obligation `BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) <= sizeof(Ip6::Address)` added by the patch. Prefix lengths that require more than 16 bytes therefore survive validation.
root_cause.note: Because this predicate returns true for the staged overlong prefix length, both the `RlocLookup()` admission pass and the later `AddPrefix()` recheck accept the same malformed prefix before `AddHasRoute()` persists it in leader network-data state.

parser_admitted.description: The received frame reaches the leader-side Server Data handler with a Thread Network Data TLV present, so nested network-data registration parsing proceeds.

coarse_trace.summary: The leader-side Server Data handler extracts the attacker's `ThreadNetworkDataTlv` from the saved message and forwards it to `RegisterNetworkData()` together with a peer RLOC16 derived from the sender address.
Before any storage, `RegisterNetworkData()` re-validates the malformed Prefix TLV and only admits the crashing path when the `HasRoute` entry matches that derived peer RLOC16.

Because `PrefixTlv::IsValid()` omits the 16-byte `Ip6::Address` bound, the same malformed prefix survives both `RlocLookup()` admission and `AddPrefix()`'s second validation, after which `AddHasRoute()` copies it into persistent leader network-data state.

The `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA` notification drives `HandleNetworkDataUpdateRouter()`, which selects `tlvs[] = {Tlv::kNetworkData}`, builds the 16-byte multicast destination `ff02::1`, and calls `SendDataResponse()`.

That one-element TLV selector makes `SendDataResponse()` resolve neighbor/context information for the multicast destination, causing leader network-data lookup to compare the stored malformed prefix against the stack `destination` address.
The persisted prefix length `0x85` rounds up to 17 bytes, and the compare loop reads `destination[16]` past the 16-byte stack buffer, producing the observed ASan stack-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: The leader-side Server Data parser extracts the attacker-controlled `ThreadNetworkDataTlv` into `networkData`. This is the first project statement that materializes the bytes later interpreted as nested Prefix TLVs.
The registration call derives a peer RLOC16 from the sender address's low 16 bits and forwards that `aRloc16` together with the raw network-data buffer into `RegisterNetworkData()`.

fine_trace.code: SuccessOrExit(error = RlocLookup(aRloc16, rlocIn, rlocStable, aTlvs, aTlvsLength, kMatchModeRloc16, /* aAllowOtherEntries */ false));
fine_trace.note: Before any leader-state update, `RegisterNetworkData()` gates the attacker-controlled TLVs through `RlocLookup(..., kMatchModeRloc16, false)`. The malformed prefix can only reach persistent network-data state if this admission pass succeeds.

fine_trace.code: return ((GetLength() >= sizeof(*this) - sizeof(NetworkDataTlv)) && (GetLength() >= BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) + sizeof(*this) - sizeof(NetworkDataTlv)));
fine_trace.note: Root cause. In `RlocLookup()`'s Prefix arm, `prefix->IsValid()` resolves to this predicate. It accepts the staged `mPrefixLength = 0x85` as long as the TLV body is long enough for 17 rounded-up prefix bytes, because it never enforces that those bytes fit inside a 16-byte IPv6 address.

fine_trace.code: if (RlocMatch(hasRouteEntry->GetRloc(), aRloc16, aMatchMode)) { aIn = true; if (hasRoute->IsStable()) { aStable = true; } } else { VerifyOrExit(aAllowOtherEntries, error = OT_ERROR_FAILED); }
fine_trace.note: The crashing path takes the `HasRoute` admission arm. With `aAllowOtherEntries` set to false in step 3, this prefix only survives registration if its `HasRoute` entry matches the peer-derived `aRloc16`; a mismatch aborts before any storage happens.

After `AddNetworkData()` reaches the incoming top-level Prefix TLV, `AddPrefix()` re-runs the same vulnerable validity check. The overlong prefix must pass this second predicate before its sub-TLVs are processed and stored.
Inside the prefix's sub-TLV loop, the recognized `HasRoute` sub-TLV is dispatched into `AddHasRoute()` rather than ignored or rejected.

fine_trace.code: dstPrefix = reinterpret_cast<PrefixTlv *>(mTlvs + mLength); Insert(reinterpret_cast<uint8_t *>(dstPrefix), sizeof(PrefixTlv) + BitVectorBytes(aPrefix.GetPrefixLength())); dstPrefix->Init(aPrefix.GetDomainId(), aPrefix.GetPrefixLength(), aPrefix.GetPrefix());
fine_trace.note: AddHasRoute allocates or extends a leader-side `PrefixTlv`, copies the attacker-controlled prefix length and prefix bytes into `mTlvs`, and appends the route entry. The malformed prefix is now persistent leader network-data state rather than transient message data.
Publishing the updated leader network data raises `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA`, propagating the persisted malformed prefix into the asynchronous state-change path.
When the queued notifier callback processes the network-data-change flag on this full-thread-device leader instance, it routes execution into `HandleNetworkDataUpdateRouter()`.
This handler materializes a one-element TLV selector containing only `Tlv::kNetworkData`, so the later response path must enter `SendDataResponse()`'s network-data case.

fine_trace.code: memset(&destination, 0, sizeof(destination)); destination.mFields.m16[0] = HostSwap16(0xff02); destination.mFields.m16[7] = HostSwap16(0x0001);
fine_trace.note: The handler builds the 16-byte stack `Ip6::Address destination` for multicast `ff02::1`. ASan later identifies this exact stack object as the overread buffer.
The unsolicited Data Response call forwards both the one-element `tlvs` selector and the 16-byte `destination` buffer into `SendDataResponse()`.

fine_trace.code: case Tlv::kNetworkData: neighbor = GetNeighbor(aDestination); stableOnly = neighbor != NULL ? !neighbor->IsFullNetworkData() : false; SuccessOrExit(error = AppendNetworkData(*message, stableOnly));
fine_trace.note: Iterating over caller-supplied `aTlvs`, the single value `Tlv::kNetworkData` selects the branch that resolves neighbor information for the multicast destination before appending network data.
Leader network-data lookup iterates stored prefixes and passes both the persisted attacker-controlled prefix length and the 16-byte destination-address byte array into `PrefixMatch()`.
PrefixMatch rounds the persisted `aLength` of `0x85` up to 17 bytes, which already exceeds the 16-byte extent of an `Ip6::Address`.

Sink. The compare loop runs for `i < 17`; when `i == 16`, `b[i]` reads one byte past the 16-byte `destination` buffer carried into `GetContext()`. ASan reports the first out-of-bounds read at this exact statement.

poc.trigger: The saved `poc` radio frame is consumed by the Stage 01 ARVO-built `radio-receive-done-fuzzer`. The harness enables Thread, makes the instance leader, calls `otPlatRadioReceiveDone()`, and then processes queued tasklets until the crash occurs.

format.name: IEEE 802.15.4 radio frame carrying Thread Server Data
format.contract: A single crafted radio frame that reaches `HandleServerData()` with a `ThreadNetworkDataTlv` (`0x0a`, length `0x23`) whose nested stable `PrefixTlv` starts `0x03 0x21 0x20 0x85`, so `mPrefixLength` is `0x85`. On the crashing path, that same prefix must also contain a `HasRoute` sub-TLV whose entry matches the peer RLOC16 derived from `aMessageInfo.mPeerAddr.mFields.m16[7]`; otherwise `RlocLookup(..., false)` or the later `AddPrefix()` recheck stops registration before `AddHasRoute()` persists the malformed prefix and the queued `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA` path compares it against the 16-byte `ff02::1` destination buffer.
